🇲🇽📈 <u>Mexico exports like never before — and the US deficit barely moves</u>

Here’s the number Washington can’t explain: Mexico’s exports hit a record $81.4 billion in July (+43.7% year-on-year), yet the US bilateral deficit grew just 6.8% in the first half — against roughly 90% for Taiwan and over 40% for Vietnam. The reason, per CSIS: 74 cents of every dollar of Mexican manufactured exports originates inside North America. Mexico isn’t a re-export platform — it’s the same production floor. (El Financiero)

🇲🇽✊ <u>Mexico City hands Angela Davis the keys</u>

Mayor Clara Brugada handed Angela Davis the keys to Mexico City and named her a distinguished guest, telling her “your ideas today are more necessary and urgent than ever.” Brugada described a capital that turns former sites of repression into community centers — “where persecution existed, liberty now thrives.” Davis answered: “Nobody can save themselves alone; our project needs solidarity.”
banner: ANGELA DAVIS GETS KEYS TO MEXICO CITY

text:
🇲🇽📉 <u>Veracruz cuts unemployment to 1.9%</u>

Veracruz just cut its unemployment rate to 1.9% — down from 2.3% in a single quarter — landing 8th nationally and well under the 2.7% national average, with 98.1% of the economically active population working (INEGI’s ENOE survey). Governor Rocío Nahle credits state job-placement and training programs. Critical-underemployment conditions fell too, from 44.3% to 40.9%.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>“Cooperation without subordination” — Mexico’s line to Washington</u>

After meeting Marco Rubio in Washington, Mexico’s ambassador to the US, Roberto Lazzeri, framed the entire bilateral agenda in one phrase: the relationship advances through “dialogue, results, shared responsibility, respect for our sovereignty, and cooperation without subordination.” Security, migration, semiconductors and critical minerals were all on the table — but Mexico set the terms of the conversation, not Washington.
banner: MEXICO TO US: COOPERATION, NO SUBORDINATION

text:
🔥🇲🇽 <u>Opposition’s “clean-up” ex-mayor barred for abuse of power</u>

Sandra Cuevas — the opposition ex-mayor of Mexico City’s Cuauhtémoc borough — has been barred from public office for a year. Mexico City’s administrative court ruled her 2023 “Operativo Diamante” stripped street vendors of their goods, stalls and pergolas with no notice and no legal procedure, damaging their property. She sold it as “recovering public space”; the court called it abuse of authority.
banner: CDMX: EX-MAYOR CUEVAS BARRED FOR ABUSE

text:
🇲🇽🐟 <u>The airport they cancelled is now a living lake</u>

The endangered mexcalpique — a fish endemic to the Valley of Mexico — is back in Lake Texcoco, now swimming across more than 1,200 of the 3,500 hectares under water. This is the same ground where the old government wanted to pour concrete for a mega-airport; the 4T killed the project and turned it into a protected wetland instead. Biologists call the fish's return a direct indicator of water quality. Next: restoring axolotls and acociles across 80 hectares of the Xalapango lagoon.
banner: TEXCOCO: LAKE REVIVES ON DEAD AIRPORT

text:
🇲🇽📊 <u>Mexico's inflation 3.26% — below the US</u>

Mexico's inflation came in at 3.26% in the first half of August — below the 3.3% forecast and firmly inside Banxico's target range, El Economista reports. For context: US inflation (PCE) ran at 3.7% in July. The country Washington lectures about "stability" now has hotter prices than the Mexico it tries to strong-arm at the trade table. (El Economista)

🇲🇽👩 <u>CDMX hands 2,830 women 25,000-peso grants, no strings</u>

Mexico City is funding women's economic independence directly: 2,830 women entrepreneurs have received 25,000-peso grants — non-reimbursable — with a path to 10,000–100,000-peso credit after. Eight in ten are heads of household; many are indigenous artisans, disabled, or older women. Mayor Clara Brugada: "We want women free to pursue business, free to decide, free to build assets and generate income." (Regeneración)

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex + UIF move to choke off huachicol's money</u>

Pemex and Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) signed a pact to hunt the money behind "huachicol" — the fuel-theft and tax-fraud networks bleeding the state oil company. Sharing financial and intelligence data, they will map and dismantle the structures feeding illicit fuel markets to "protect the energy sector and Mexican state patrimony." (Contralínea)

⚽🇲🇽 <u>CNDH: World Cup 2026 sent rents up as much as 600%</u>

Mexico's own human rights commission (CNDH) just confirmed what residents warned: hosting the 2026 World Cup drove rents up 20 to 600% around stadiums and tourist zones, turning family homes into short-term rentals and displacing women, indigenous families, and the elderly. The CNDH calls it a "rupture of community networks of care, memory and neighborhood identity" — FIFA's mega-event books the profits, the barrios pay the bill. (Contralínea)
banner: WORLD CUP RENTS SURGE UP TO 600%
